summary: Client keepalive drift causes trailing ellipsis and duplicated suffix on stream resume
description: Issue summary: Customers reported that long streaming responses (SSE and websocket) occasionally finish with a trailing ellipsis (...) and then, after the client reconnect/resume, a duplicated final clause or sentence is appended. Impact: user-visible duplicated suffix or hanging punctuation in final output that confuses downstream post-processing and fails strict JSON validators for structured responses. Observed with enterprise customer behind an aggressive corporate proxy and mobile webview clients.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Start a long multi-paragraph generation request using the streaming endpoint for redwood/ggml-7b-chat with temperature=0.7 and max_tokens=800.
2) Let stream emit for ~20–40s until the model returns the closing paragraph and likely a final punctuation mark.
3) Trigger a transient network change on the client (corporate proxy rebind or mobile network suspend) causing a keepalive gap of ~12–18s.
4) Client reconnects and sends resume token / session id; server emits remaining fragments and occasionally emits a duplicate of the last sentence or an extra ellipsis then duplicate suffix.
5) Reproduces reliably behind Acme Payments' corp-proxy which has an idle-teardown of 10s when reauthenticating.

investigation_notes: Initial triage (Support): confirmed multiple occurrences from same customer in us-east over 3 distinct days. Pattern: short-lived network gaps of ~10–20s followed by resume, duplicates only on longest streams.
Hypothesis A: KV-cache re-priming race where resumed worker replays buffered tail while prior worker also emits trailing fragment (double-emit).
Hypothesis B: Edge-proxy keepalive extension mismatch causes client to receive a heartbeat-only chunk (ellipsis) interpreted by SDK as content, then resumed content appended leading to duplication.

SRE reproduction: simulated proxy-teardown at 10s while streaming long responses; reproduced duplicate tail when proxy dropped connection and resume routed request to a different worker with overlapping session state.

Trace analysis: tx-5543 shows two downstream emits (chunk 457 and chunk 458) with same choice payload and consecutive sequence ids; both workers reported chunk emission for same session id due to race on resume-claim.

Root cause narrowed: race during resume claim across serving nodes when proxy rebind causes an ephemeral reconnect; resume path allowed a second worker to re-emit cached tail before exclusive resume-claim was fully reconciled in the control plane.

Customer environment note: Acme's corp-proxy performs TLS re-termination + 401 reauth flow which triggers connection close and immediate reconnects; their idle-teardown (10s) is shorter than our resume-claim lock timeout in some code paths.
Repro notes: duplication more likely when final chunk is small (ellipsis or short clause) because the SDK merges heartbeat-like fragments into content and treats them as partials.

resolution: Root cause: race condition in session resume where two workers could emit a cached trailing fragment when corporate proxy rebind closes the original socket. Fix: added an optimistic resume-claim lock in the control plane and tightened the session tail GC window; also added defensive de-duplication in the serving runtime for back-to-back identical tail emits. Rollout: hotfix canary in us-east on 2026-03-11 09:30 UTC, global rollout completed 2026-03-11 18:00 UTC. Customer instructed to adjust proxy idle teardown to >15s or enable client resume backoff as mitigation. Monitoring: alert created stream-resume-duplicate-rate >0.1% per minute with dashboard link.
